title: Ask what an encounter keeps
storyboard: The crab turns toward a beacon or mushroom; a screen can remove a candidate from view. Bring distance comparisons, conditions and the previous hall's distinction between commanded movement and physical response. Before a meal starts, keep candidate positions fixed and insert the screen: predict what selection may change and what completed-meal history cannot. Read the supplied selector and feeding record to check that account. The learner need not rebuild steering, legs or an event system. The five-meal stop is authored, while the meaning of this apparent relationship remains open to discussion. Keep the collision carts as a separate, optional comparison with an explicit one-dimensional model. Carry a distinction between present eligibility, retained events and an interpretation of agency; none alone establishes the others.
storyboard_short: Keep Arena a comparison. Reuse distances, conditions and commanded-body distinctions. Before feeding starts, hold positions fixed, insert the screen and predict selection versus completed-meal history. Read the supplied selector and event record; build no new controller. The five-meal stop is authored. Keep collision carts a separate model and interpretation open. Carry a distinction between eligibility, retained events and attributed agency.
brings: the distinction between a current input and retained state
Legs' comparison of commanded and physically supported movement
learns: a candidate must remain eligible before distance can select it
a completed-event count differs from the current target
an authored threshold and an interpretation of agency answer different questions
carries: An inspectable account of a choice, the event history it retains and the interpretive claims that remain open.
supplied: lesson_crab's existing eligible-candidate selector and line-of-sight query
museum beacon, mushroom, screen and controls
feeding events, steering and gait; the separate analytic collision-cart comparison
review_note: Change the former make obligation to reflect: the current final/tutorial support an encounter and source comparison, not a prerequisite to author a new selector, gait or event framework. Selection uses a strict six-metre candidate range and a supplied visibility test; active feeding and temporary ignoring affect when selection resumes. The five completed meals trigger an authored stop, not learned policy. The carts display a supplied analytic elastic-collision account rather than measuring the crab's collisions. Keep critical interpretation available without presenting friendship, intent or conservation as facts proved by target selection.
independent_check: Start before a meal is underway. With candidate positions unchanged, insert the screen and predict which candidate remains eligible. Explain why an occlusion may change the selected target but cannot itself increase the completed-meal count; use the existing rules to check both claims.
change_reason: The encounter can develop a careful reading of agency and retained state. An additional implementation obligation would crowd that work and blur its distinction from the separate collision model.
